new_statements.quote: Fleming did not report anything about length and tone. But in the present study contrastive length of both vocalic and consonantal and two distinct tone levels (high and low) are found. In this study, tone is not treated because our purpose now is to show a non-linear account of the segmental phonology of the language that was previously described linearly. [note 2, p. 15:] The two tone levels are identified on the basis of the following pairs of wards [sic] (´ marks high tone; ` marks low tone): kárò 'horn' / kànò 'dog'; gínò 'spear' / kíšó 'hand(palm)'; màngó 'heavy' / yòngò 'wind'; s'àllò 'porcupine' / s'úlló 'small'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The only dedicated phonology of Anfillo reports that the language has two contrastive tone levels (H and L), shown by lexical minimal pairs on disyllabic nouns/adjectives (e.g. kárò 'horn' vs kànò 'dog'), and explicitly excludes tone from its analysis. It says nothing whatever about word stress: no rule of stress placement, no claim that stress is absent, no mention of prominence. So there is no stress placement rule to extract; the language is described as tonal.
new_statements.exceptions: None; tone is not analysed beyond the minimal-pair note (both HL, LL, LH and HH patterns appear in the examples, so tone is lexical, not fixed).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: the tone pairs are isolated citation forms (mostly disyllabic nouns and adjectives); no phrase-level remarks. The thesis is a segmental study in a non-linear framework and does not contain a suprasegmental section.
new_statements.identity_note: The thesis describes Anfillo = Southern Mao of Grottanelli (1940) and Bender (1971), spoken at the northern edge of the then Gambella region (Anfillo woreda, West Wellega); it states there is no significant dialectal variation. Same variety as Glottolog anfi1235 / ISO myo. Not to be confused with Northern Mao / Diddessa Mao (Mao branch), for which AAU also holds theses.

sources.locator: p. 4 (PDF p. 15), §1.3 Previous Studies; note 2 on p. 15 (PDF p. 26)
sources.note: Whole thesis is segmental phonology (consonants, vowels, syllable structure, processes); no stress/suprasegmental section. In §1.3 (p. 4) it states that contrastive vowel and consonant length and two distinct tone levels (high and low) are found, and that tone is deliberately not treated; note 2 (p. 15) gives eight tone minimal pairs. The words stress/accent/prominence never occur (grep of full scanned).
